reviews.one_line_contribution: A regime-transplant difference-in-differences diagnostic claiming that instructions evolved by a reflective optimizer while a retrieved memory bank is injected become dependent on that specific bank (so the reported optimizer+memory gain is bank-conditional rather than owned), plus a counterfactual-replay routing rule (CCR) that sends memory-caused training failures to the write path instead of the instruction reflector.
reviews.closest_prior_work: On the mechanism, the proposal is right that CANTANTE (2605.13295) and Environment-Grounded APO (2606.17838) are the nearest threats, and it honestly concedes the counterfactual-replay signal as prior art; B9 is a fair gradient-free stand-in for UCOB/HiMPO. The larger unacknowledged threat is to the object the proposal actually claims as novel — the transplant/DiD diagnostic. 'Optimize under regime A, evaluate under regime B' is a train/test regime swap, i.e. the standard prompt-transfer ablation that MIPRO/DSPy-lineage work and 'Teach Better or Show Smarter?' already run in the instruction-vs-exemplar setting, and the RAG literature routinely reports optimized prompts degrading when the retriever or demonstration pool is swapped. Substituting 'self-editing experience bank' for 'bootstrapped demonstration set' changes the artifact but not the experimental move. Conceptually, 'co-adaptation between two jointly fitted components, removable by dropout' is the classical dropout argument, which is why B4 is the theoretically motivated fix and CCR the elaborate one. The claim 'none of them runs the transplant' is also precisely the claim the proposal admits it never searched for (the OpenReview query it could not run), so it rests on assertion.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline quantity is not identified. DiD = [R_mem@T_mem − R_mem@T_nomem] − [R_nomem@T_mem − R_nomem@T_nomem]. The second bracket is, by this track's own prior measurement, already known to be negative: injecting the full k=7 bank into an unadapted prompt fixed zero items and broke six to seven (McNemar p=0.031/0.016). A DiD of +5 points or more can therefore be produced entirely by memory harming the memory-free instruction, with literally zero co-adaptation in the R_mem instruction — and P1's own prose gloss ('instructions optimized with memory lose more when memory is removed than memory-free instructions gain from having it') is satisfied trivially when the memory-free instruction *loses* from having memory. The proposal never states that the first bracket must be positive, never reports a precondition on it, and never separates 'k=7 injection harms any prompt' (a published result of this track) from 'this instruction has absorbed this bank' (the new claim). This compounds with a second, related problem: R_mem is deliberately trained at k=7, the exact injection volume the track already showed to be harmful and already showed to be fixable by cutting to k=3. So the co-adaptation being studied may be co-adaptation to a known pathology, and the most likely empirical outcome is that B10 (train at k=2) removes the effect — which the proposal itself concedes collapses the routing story. P2, the 'sharp, disagreeable' claim, is worse off still: a gain cannot be shown to be rented if there is no gain. P2 asserts R_mem's advantage over R_nomem at T_shift falls to ≤1 point, but nothing in the design establishes that this advantage exists at T_mem in the first place, and the track's prior data suggests it may not. As written, P2 risks being vacuously 'confirmed' by an advantage that was never there. Secondarily, the mechanism separation in P6 — the thing that distinguishes CCR from a blind regularizer, and the paper's actual method contribution — rests on B9, B10 and B5 at 3 seeds each, with no MDE stated for 3-seed conditions; with the proposal's own between-seed SD of 2.0-2.5 points, a 3-seed contrast cannot support a claim like 'B9 captures less than half of CCR's interaction reduction' or 'B4/B10 lose ≥2 points at T_mem relative to CCR'. The MDE section carefully powers the claim the authors expect to win and leaves the claims that would kill the method underpowered.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a precondition, reported before anything else, on all four Part 1 cells separately rather than only their contrast: state and test that memory injection at the chosen k actually helps (or at least does not harm) an unadapted and an R_nomem instruction, and choose k accordingly. If the second DiD bracket is negative, drop the DiD as primary and use a quantity that cannot be manufactured by injection harm — e.g. the within-R_mem T_mem→T_shift drop benchmarked against a bank-swap-matched control, with the R_mem@T_mem − R_mem@T_nomem single difference reported with its sign. (2) Report P1 at both k=7 and k=3, so the diagnostic is not confounded with the already-known volume pathology, and specify the evaluation k for B10 (as written, B10 trains at k=2 and is evaluated at T_mem k=7, which is itself a train/test regime mismatch and stacks the deck against the strongest competing intervention). (3) Add the volume-matched placebo optimization regime described in missing_baseline; without it, 'memory-referential clauses' in P3 and the DiD in P1 are both consistent with adaptation to 7 extra context items of any content. (4) Give B9 and B10 five paired seeds and publish their MDEs, or strip the numeric thresholds out of P6 and state it qualitatively; the paper's mechanism claim should not be the least-powered comparison in it. (5) The track brief says a methods contribution must overturn or qualify specific existing results. Run the transplant protocol on at least one re-implemented published memory+optimizer system (ACE-style joint loop is named as the motivating target), not only on the authors' own pipeline, or restate P2 explicitly as a claim about this pipeline rather than about 'published-style headline gains'. (6) Complete the OpenReview/transplant search and resolve 2605.28732, whose title covers Part 2 directly.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. First, a volume-matched placebo optimization regime — R_shuf: optimize with the same k=7 injection slot filled by shuffled or task-irrelevant items of matched token volume, then transplant. The proposal lists a shuffled-bank check only as an evaluation-time sanity control, not as a training regime, so nothing in the design separates 'the instruction adapted to this bank's content' from 'the instruction adapted to having a long retrieved block in context'. Every Part 1 result and the P3 clause correlation survive equally under the null hypothesis of pure volume adaptation. Second, multi-bank / bank-resampling optimization: optimize R_mem while alternating between two or more independently written banks and evaluate on a third. This is the standard domain-randomization answer to P2's shift claim, is cheaper than CCR, and is not the same as B4 (dropout randomizes memory *presence*, not bank *identity*, so it cannot teach bank-invariance, only memory-optionality). A reviewer will ask why the obvious fix for bank-conditionality — train on more than one bank — was not the first thing tried, and if it works, CCR is unnecessary for the paper's own headline robustness claim.
reviews.preprint_collision: The best part of the submission, and unusually honest: nine items named with IDs, an explicit concession that the counterfactual-replay signal is prior art, HiMPO/CANTANTE/UCOB correctly identified as mechanism ancestors, UCOB promoted into a baseline (B9) rather than argued away, and ACE reframed as the motivating target. That is more collision work than most submissions do. But it is thorough exactly where the proposal no longer claims novelty and thin exactly where it does. The authors state plainly that both search sessions were rate-limited before any targeted query on 'transplant / difference-in-differences evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation' could be run — that is, the one search that bears on the claimed novel object was never executed, and the proposal itself flags this as the least-verified load-bearing item. Two further entries are unresolved: 'Tracing and Attributing Errors in LLM Memory Systems' (2605.28732), whose title covers Part 2's attribution problem and for which only a reference list was retrieved, and the ICLR 2026 counterfactual-RAG poster whose abstract was never obtained. Per the standard that an unsearched claim of novelty is a weakness rather than a neutral: the mechanism half is properly cleared and correctly de-claimed, the diagnostic half is unsearched, and the diagnostic half is the entire remaining contribution. Candor about the gap is worth credit in the clarity and integrity dimension; it does not substitute for the search.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A transplant / difference-in-differences diagnostic (optimize instructions under memory-present vs. memory-absent regimes, then cross-evaluate under absent / same-bank / shifted-bank / truncated regimes) claiming that reflectively-optimized instructions silently absorb the specific memory bank they were tuned against, so that reported optimizer+memory gains are bank-conditional; plus a counterfactual-replay routing rule (CCR) that sends memory-caused failures to the bank rather than the instruction. The proposal explicitly concedes the counterfactual-replay signal itself is prior art, so the novel object is the diagnostic and the bank-conditionality claim, not the fix.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two different works threaten the two halves. For the fix: CANTANTE (2605.13295) and UCOB (2606.29502) already do contrastive / two-view counterfactual credit attribution over context components, and the proposal itself demotes UCOB's mechanism to a baseline (B9); if B9 matches B6, CCR is a gradient-free reimplementation of published machinery and the method claim is gone by the proposal's own pre-commitment. Environment-Grounded APO (2606.17838) already runs failure-source attribution (context module vs. agent behavior) inside a prompt-optimization loop; the distinction offered — its Descriptor is a fixed perception module rather than a self-editing bank — is a difference in the object attributed over, not in the attribution method, and is thin for a main-track novelty argument. For the diagnostic, the real threat is not an agent-memory paper at all but the instruction-vs-exemplar decomposition line (MIPRO; 'Teach Better or Show Smarter?') combined with the ordinary, universally known fact that an artifact optimized under regime A is best under regime A. The transplant design is a standard train/test-regime-mismatch 2x2; calling its outcome 'co-adaptation' renames a familiar result unless the proposal can show the memory-specific DiD exceeds a generic regime-matching DiD, which it never attempts.
reviews.strongest_objection: P1 is close to unfalsifiable in the interesting direction, and P2's premise is contradicted by the track's own data. (a) The headline DiD = [acc(R_mem@T_mem) - acc(R_mem@T_nomem)] - [acc(R_nomem@T_mem) - acc(R_nomem@T_nomem)] is positive whenever optimization does anything at all, because each instruction is evaluated in the regime it was selected in. The plan contains no control that separates 'the instruction encoded compensations for Bank_A' from 'any optimized artifact degrades off its training regime.' The instruction-paraphrase control tests prompt fragility, not regime matching; the memory-referential-clause readout (P3) is a Spearman correlation over n=10 runs from a subjective judge — at rho=0.5, n=10, that is not distinguishable from chance and cannot carry the mechanistic burden. So a confirmed P1 is uninformative and a refuted P1 is the only outcome that teaches anything, which is the wrong way round for a paper whose primary claim is P1. (b) The research track's own measured starting position is that injecting the full bank at k=7 fixed zero items and broke six to seven. If that reproduces in E1, then acc(R_mem@T_mem) - acc(R_mem@T_nomem) is near zero or negative and there is no headline gain to be 'rented': P2, the sharp and disagreeable claim the proposal rests its significance on, becomes vacuous, and no gate anywhere in the plan detects this before the budget is spent. (c) P2 is operationalized as a ratio ('R_mem instructions drop at least twice as much'), and the denominator is R_nomem's T_mem-to-T_shift drop, which for an instruction that never mentions memory should be near zero — making the criterion either trivially satisfied or undefined. (d) The power arithmetic assumes a between-optimizer-seed SD of 2.0-2.5 points, but the track reports re-scoring/null-replicate drift of 5-14 points in this exact setting; if the larger figure is what the null optimizer replicate returns, the paired-seed MDE is roughly 8+ points, P5 (a 5-point reduction) is undetectable, and the pre-registered cut order does not rescue it because it cuts scope, not variance.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes, all cheap relative to the 107k-episode budget. (1) Add a memory-irrelevant regime-shift control: optimize under R_mem and evaluate under a perturbation of comparable magnitude that has nothing to do with memory (step-limit change, tool-output formatting change, or a distractor-passage swap), and pre-register that the memory DiD must significantly exceed this generic regime-matching DiD. Without that floor, P1 measures overfitting-to-training-regime, which nobody disputes. (2) Add an explicit go/no-go gate before Part 2 and Part 3: on the unoptimized prompt, B1 minus B0 at T_mem must show memory conferring a positive gain of at least the stated MDE; if the track's zero-fix/six-break result reproduces, P2 is void and the paper should be rewritten as 'memory does not help, so there is nothing to co-adapt to' rather than reporting a rented-gain result with no rent. (3) Restate P2 as an absolute three-way interaction (regime x bank x seed) with a CI, not a ratio of drops, and report R_nomem's drop with its own CI. (4) Run the null optimizer replicate as a pilot and set the MDEs from the observed between-seed SD before committing the seed counts, instead of assuming 2.0-2.5 in the face of the cited 5-14 point drift. Additionally, the paper's motivating target (ACE-style joint offline prompt optimization plus online memory adaptation) is never actually run — B3 is a home-built composition with a frozen bank — so the claim that published gains are bank-conditional is not tested on any published system; either run one genuine joint loop or scope the claim to the reimplementation.
reviews.missing_baseline: Bank randomization during optimization: run the optimizer with memory always present but with the injected items drawn each minibatch from a rotating pool of banks (or a resampled subset of Bank_A), and/or perform candidate selection on validation minibatches that use a held-out bank. This is domain randomization applied to the demonstration slot, it is the first thing a competent engineer would try after reading the diagnostic, and it plausibly removes bank-conditionality without sacrificing any of the memory's contribution — which is exactly the outcome the proposal asserts only CCR can achieve (P6). B4 randomizes only presence/absence and B10 only volume; neither varies bank content, so neither covers this. A second omission: a retrieval-gating / abstention baseline where the agent decides per step whether to admit retrieved items — the track lists the injection budget as a first-class decision variable, and B10's fixed k=2 cap is a strawman version of it. A third, cheaper one: instructions optimized with memory but early-stopped or candidate-selected on T_shift-style validation.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually diligent on the axis that does not carry the novelty and empty on the axis that does — and the proposal says so itself, which is honest but is still a weakness, not a neutral. Ten-plus specific 2026 preprints are named and correctly triaged for the counterfactual-credit mechanism (HiMPO 2606.16285, CANTANTE 2605.13295, UCOB 2606.29502, Memory-R2 2605.21768, TreeMem 2605.04811, 2605.30227, Env-Grounded APO 2606.17838), and the author concedes the mechanism as prior art. But the single load-bearing novel move — a transplant / difference-in-differences evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation and bank substitution — was never searched: both sessions were rate-limited before the targeted queries ran. Two live residual risks are flagged and unresolved: 'Tracing and Attributing Errors in LLM Memory Systems' (2605.28732), retrieved at title level only, is a direct-sounding collision, and the ICLR 2026 counterfactual-RAG poster's abstract was never retrieved. Beyond what the author lists, the check never touches the adjacent literature most likely to have pre-empted the diagnostic: in-context-learning work on prompts overfitting to their exemplar set, and RAG work measuring a model's reliance on injected context versus its parametric behavior — both routinely report the exact cross-regime evaluation being proposed as the new object. Net: novelty on the fix is conceded away, and novelty on the diagnostic rests on a search that was not performed.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A transplant/difference-in-differences measurement showing that instructions produced by a reflective prompt optimizer under an injected memory bank become conditionally dependent on that specific bank (so the reported optimizer+memory gain is bank-conditional rather than a property of the instruction), plus a counterfactual-replay routing rule (CCR) that sends memory-attributable failures to the write path instead of the instruction reflector.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two fronts. For the fix: Environment-Grounded APO for game agents (2606.17838) already runs failure attribution between a context-providing module and the agent's own prompt inside a prompt-optimization loop, and CANTANTE (2605.13295) already does contrastive trajectory-level attribution over workflow components with a prompted judge; the proposal concedes both, so CCR is an application of an existing signal to a new slot, and B9 (soft two-view) is by the authors' own account the strongest baseline precisely because it is what those papers imply. For the diagnostic, the threat is not a single paper but the standard train-regime/test-regime mismatch analysis: MIPRO/GEPA-style optimizers are known to overfit the evaluation configuration they were scored under, and Adv-ICL-style 'w/o demonstration' ablations already measure sensitivity to removing the exemplar slot. Running that same ablation on prompts optimized under two regimes is a small design increment, and the authors' rebuttal ('they ablate at evaluation time within a single optimization regime') concedes exactly how small it is. The specific arXiv item that would kill it (a transplant/DiD evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation) is the one query the proposal admits it never ran.
reviews.strongest_objection: The DiD in P1 is sign-ambiguous and, in the direction the authors need, close to guaranteed by construction. DiD = [R_mem@T_mem - R_mem@T_nomem] - [R_nomem@T_mem - R_nomem@T_nomem] is positive under two opposite mechanisms: (i) R_mem instructions collapse when memory is removed (co-adaptation, the paper's story), or (ii) R_nomem instructions collapse when memory is forced on them at k=7 (memory harming a prompt never written to consume it). The track's own starting position says mechanism (ii) is real and large in this exact setup: k=7 injection fixed zero items and broke six to seven. So the more likely driver of a >=5-point interaction is the baseline arm degrading, not the treated arm being brittle, and the plan never pre-registers the simple-effect decomposition that would separate them. Compounding this: the same prior result undercuts P6. If memory's in-distribution contribution at k=7 is zero or negative, then B4 memory dropout and B10 k=2 capping cost nothing at T_mem -- indeed B10 is the configuration the track already found removes the harm -- and P6's prediction that they pay >=2 points of T_mem accuracy relative to B6 fails, at which point the authors' own refutation clause fires and the method claim reduces to 'a blind regularizer would have done it.' Separately, 'co-adaptation' is not what is tested: HELD FIXED freezes Bank_A during optimization, so R_mem is unidirectional prompt overfitting to a static context, while the motivating target (ACE) has a bank that is being rewritten concurrently -- the control list even contains a 'frozen-memory ablation during R_mem optimization,' which is vacuous if the bank was frozen all along and contradicts HELD FIXED if it was not. Finally, P2's effect size is a free parameter: the T_mem->T_shift drop is set by how far the Bank_B task-family mix is pushed, there is no calibration of shift severity, and the 'drops at least twice as much' ratio is unstable because the R_nomem denominator is expected to be near zero.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Pre-register the two simple effects, not just the interaction: require acc(R_mem@T_nomem) < acc(R_nomem@T_nomem) by a stated margin as a necessary condition for reading a positive DiD as co-adaptation, and report the interaction decomposed into both arms with fix/break counts. 2) Gate the whole program on a measured memory contribution: report acc(B1)-acc(B0) at k=7 on E1 first; if it is <=0 (as the track's prior result predicts), P6 as written is dead on arrival and the B4/B10 comparison must be restated in terms of shift robustness only. 3) Make the primary R_mem arm a genuinely co-evolving one (bank edited by the write path during optimization) and demote the frozen-bank arm to the control, so the diagnostic matches the system (ACE) it claims to indict; and resolve the HELD FIXED / frozen-memory-ablation contradiction. 4) Replace the ratio form of P2 with an absolute, dose-response form: build three Bank_B variants at graded mix distance and report the drop as a function of measured shift, plus a bank-quality control (B0/B1 evaluated on each bank) so a bad bank is not read as a brittle instruction. 5) State a decision rule for the case where the interaction is large but driven by memory-referential clauses that are simply good advice under any bank -- the P3 clause analysis should be causal (ablate the memory-referential clauses from R_mem instructions and re-evaluate) rather than a 10-point Spearman correlation, which is underpowered as specified.
reviews.missing_baseline: Cheap re-optimization under the target regime. The 'rented gain' framing only bites if renting again is expensive, so a reviewer will demand: take the B3 instruction and run the same reflective optimizer for a small fraction of the budget (e.g. 100-150 rollouts) against Bank_B, then evaluate at T_shift. If a short re-optimization recovers most of the T_mem->T_shift drop at a cost far below CCR's replay overhead, P2 describes a maintenance chore rather than a failure mode, and CCR's >=3-point T_shift advantage over B3 is measured against the wrong reference. A second omission on the same axis: no condition optimizes the instruction while selecting candidates on a validation set drawn from a bank the instruction will not see at test time (regime-mixed selection over two banks), which is the obvious and nearly free robustness fix distinct from B4's within-bank dropout. Also absent: any arm where the instruction is allowed to reference the injection budget as a decision variable, despite the track's own finding that volume is the causal lever -- B10 fixes k=2 by fiat rather than letting the agent choose.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually good -- nine named items, an explicit concession that the counterfactual-replay signal is prior art (HiMPO 2606.16285, CANTANTE 2605.13295, UCOB 2606.29502), and the promotion of UCOB's idea into an explicit baseline (B9). I credit that honesty. But it fails exactly where it matters. After the concession, novelty rests entirely on the transplant/DiD diagnostic and the P2 bank-conditionality claim, and the proposal states that both search sessions were rate-limited before any targeted query on 'transplant / difference-in-differences evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation' could be run. So the single load-bearing novelty claim is the one item never searched, and two directly adjacent items -- 'Tracing and Attributing Errors in LLM Memory Systems' (2605.28732) and the ICLR 2026 'Counterfactual Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation' poster -- are logged as unretrieved abstracts. By the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is a real deduction, not a formality: a prompt-optimization robustness paper with a memory-ablation transplant table in its appendix is a plausible 2026 preprint, and the authors themselves flag it as their concentrated novelty risk. The search must be completed before this is submittable; the rest of the collision check is strong enough that finishing it is a small amount of work.
